paras_en: The dollar weakened on Thursday (the 8th), pausing the rise in Eurozone government bond yields, while market expectations for the Fed's rate path this year remained largely unchanged.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, fell 0.08% to 102.17 after briefly climbing to 102.46.
The euro rose 0.08% against the dollar to $1.1204, after dipping intraday to $1.1171.
Eurozone sovereign yields surged again as oil price spikes heightened inflation concerns, prompting investors to continue selling bonds of heavily indebted countries such as France and Italy.
However, as the yield rally cooled, the euro recovered from its intraday low. France's 10‑year yield rose 2.7 basis points to 4.8873%, briefly reaching 4.9685% during the session.
The impact on France was especially pronounced as investors closely examined its debt size, budget deficit, and political outlook ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
In Spain, unions announced on Wednesday a nationwide general strike on November 11 to protest housing issues, a protest taking place only weeks before an early election.
Fed signals cautious rate‑hike stance

Market expectations for a rate hike at the Fed's later policy meeting this month remain low. After the Fed released minutes of its latest meeting on Wednesday, officials said inflation remains the biggest risk to the economic outlook, and analysts said the minutes offered no surprise signals.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that further rate hikes may still be needed to bring inflation down to the Fed's 2% target, but he also noted that the pace of hikes is “flexible,” leaving room to pause at the upcoming October meeting.
Waller's comments echoed remarks from other Fed officials last week, who all signaled a desire to be patient on any further tightening.

Christoph Schon, head of multi‑asset investment decision research at SimCorp, said, “Most other currencies seem to move opposite to their monetary‑policy expectations, but that’s because everything has been dominated by the dollar and the Fed, and that situation has persisted over the past few weeks.”

“Interestingly, there is now another factor affecting the euro – the political crises in France and now even Spain… So this is a short‑term episode where the focus is not on rate differentials or policy, but on a very specific euro crisis that is currently influencing the currency,” he added.
Markets bet on a December hike

According to the CME FedWatch tool, the market currently assigns a 17.2% probability that the Fed will raise rates by at least 25 basis points this month, down slightly from 24.4% a week ago. However, investors see an 81.2% chance of a hike at the December meeting.

After Waller’s remarks, a Goldman Sachs analyst wrote that they still expect a 25‑basis‑point hike in December and lowered the probability of no hike, interpreting Waller’s comments as a shift toward a more hawkish stance.
In an even more hawkish tone, Alberto Musalem, president of St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank, said the U.S. central bank needs another rate increase to bring inflation back to the 2% target.

On the data front, the U.S. Labor Department reported that initial unemployment claims fell by 2,000 to 197,000 last week, slightly below the Reuters poll forecast of 200,000, indicating the labor market remains stable.

Eurozone inflation may be higher than already elevated forecasts, but ECB policymakers have dampened market bets on a near‑term hike, with several officials on Thursday noting that, based on fundamentals, the situation is actually fairly moderate.
The widening yield gap between German bonds and those of high‑debt Eurozone members such as France and Italy has pushed the euro down to its lowest level since May 2024.

The pound rose 0.07% to $1.3219 after Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said that as global bond markets face high borrowing and rising inflation pressures, governments need to work harder to demonstrate fiscal repair capability.

The dollar fell 0.12% to ¥157.88. The Bank of Japan said rising raw‑material costs are feeding price increases into consumer goods, with some firms raising prices more frequently, showing the BOJ’s concern over expanding inflation pressures.

FOMC上個月一致投票決定將聯邦資金利率上調25個基點，為3年多來首次升息。同時，FOMC更新後的點陣圖也暗示今年還可能進一步升息。聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)則在會後記者會上表示，讓通膨回落至央行2%的目標，仍是一項重大挑戰。
會議紀要指出，「關於本次會議之後的貨幣政策前景，多數與會者認為，在今年年底前進一步上調聯邦資金利率目標區間可能是適當的。」
紀要也顯示，所有FOMC官員都支持9月升息。
不過，這份紀要公布之際，市場對FOMC本月底再次升息的預期已較9月升息後大幅下降，主要受到近期部分官員偏鴿派的談話，以及美國經濟成長、通膨與勞動市場數據的影響。
根據CME FedWatch工具，目前市場預期本月底維持利率不變的機率接近83%，高於一個月前約54%的水準。
歐元受法國財政危機拖累
美元走強另一助力是歐元周三走跌。歐元兌美元下跌0.6%，至1歐元兌1.1195美元。
隨著法國財政危機惡化，以及西班牙政治陷入僵局，歐洲大陸的市場風險情緒承受壓力。法國10年期公債殖利率已升至2000年初以來未見高點。
法國今年財政赤字預計將達國內生產毛額(GDP)的5.4%，公共債務則接近GDP的120%。
法國政府上周公布2027年預算案，目標透過削減540億歐元的支出，將財政赤字目標控制在GDP的5%。
同時，法國在明年4月與5月舉行兩輪選舉前，也面臨政治不確定性。總統大選領先者、極右派政黨國民聯盟(National Rally)候選人勒龐，以及該黨黨魁Jordan Bardella周二公布主要預算方案，目標在2032年前節省1,400億歐元。
英鎊走弱 英國30年期公債殖利率創1998年來新高
全球債券拋售潮周三蔓延至英國，英國30年期公債殖利率升至1998年1月以來最高水準。
就在一天前，英國財政大臣John Healey才與英國公債市場的主要交易商會面，即所謂的金邊債券造市者(Gilt-edged Market Makers, GEMMs)。
英國財政部表示，與會者討論了英國與全球經濟所面臨的嚴峻外部環境，包括地緣政治發展與金融市場狀況。
英鎊兌美元下跌0.5%，至1英鎊兌1.3213美元。

paras_en: The dollar strengthened on Wednesday (the 7th), rising to a near 18‑month high, buoyed by Fed meeting minutes that indicated a possible further rate hike and by the weakness of the euro and pound. The euro and pound were pressured by a renewed wave of global bond sell‑offs, bearing downward pressure.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, rose 0.4% to 102.24, briefly touching its highest level since April 9, 2025.

Forex market participants on Wednesday focused on the Fed’s September monetary policy meeting minutes. The minutes showed that most Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members think another rate hike could still be possible before the end of the year.

Last month the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, the first hike in more than three years. At the same time, the updated FOMC dot‑plot also hinted at the possibility of further hikes this year. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said in the post‑meeting press conference that bringing inflation down to the central bank’s 2% target remains a major challenge.

The minutes noted, “Regarding the monetary policy outlook after this meeting, most participants believe that a further increase in the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate before the end of this year.”
The minutes also showed that all FOMC members supported a September rate hike.

However, as the minutes were released, market expectations for another FOMC hike at the end of the month had fallen sharply from after the September hike, mainly due to recent dovish remarks by some officials and the impact of U.S. economic growth, inflation and labor market data.
According to the CME FedWatch tool, the market now sees an almost 83% probability that rates will remain unchanged at the end of the month, up from about 54% a month ago.
Euro weighed down by France’s fiscal crisis
Another boost to the dollar’s strength was the euro’s decline on Wednesday. The euro fell 0.6% against the dollar to $1.1195 per euro.

As France’s fiscal crisis deepens and Spain’s politics stall, market risk sentiment across the continent is under pressure. France’s 10‑year government bond yield has risen to its highest level since early 2000.
France’s fiscal deficit this year is projected to reach 5.4% of GDP, with public debt close to 120% of GDP.
The French government unveiled its 2027 budget last week, aiming to cut €54 billion in spending and keep the fiscal deficit target at 5% of GDP.

At the same time, France faces political uncertainty ahead of two rounds of elections in April and May next year. National Rally leader Jordan Bardella, the party’s frontrunner in the presidential race, announced on Tuesday a major budget plan targeting €140 billion in savings by 2032.
Pound weakens as UK 30‑year gilt yield hits a 1998 high
A global bond sell‑off on Wednesday spread to the UK, pushing the 30‑year gilt yield to its highest level since January 1998.
Just a day earlier, UK Treasury Secretary John Healey met with the main dealers in the gilt market, the so‑called Gilt‑edged Market Makers (GEMMs).
The Treasury said the meeting discussed the severe external environment facing the UK and global economies, including geopolitical developments and financial market conditions.
The pound fell 0.5% against the dollar to $1.3213 per pound.

paras: 新台幣今(7)日持續呈升貶互見走勢，由於台股上攻5萬點近關情怯，匯市量縮觀望氣氛也趨於濃厚，終場收在31.795元，貶值1.4分，台北外匯經紀公司成交值13.74億美元。
新台幣今日以31.8元、貶值1.9分開出後，一度升值至31.76元，但全日多處在走弱態勢，最低來到31.821元，高低價差6.1分。
觀察主要亞幣，由於美元指數強彈達0.4%，非美貨幣全面走弱，泰銖貶0.4%，星元貶逾0.2%，日元和人民幣貶0.1%左右，新台幣收貶0.04%。
統一投顧分析，儘管市場聚焦中東情勢發展，並關注本周聯準會將發布9月會議記錄，不過，IEA宣布釋放1億桶戰略儲油，短線有助油價趨向穩定。
另一方面，AI熱潮驅動企業投資與經濟穩健成長，美國9月ISM製造業新訂單加速擴張，隨著第三季財報季將在下周登場，統計機構持續上修獲利展望，有利美股多頭格局，並進一步穩固台股下檔支撐。
paras_en: The New Taiwan dollar continued a mixed up‑and‑down pattern today (the 7th), as the Taiwan stock index’s push toward the 50,000‑point mark sparked nervousness near the close. The foreign‑exchange market’s thin trading and cautious mood also intensified, and the dollar ended at NT$31.795, down 0.014, with Taipei’s foreign‑exchange brokers handling US$13.74 billion in transactions.
The New Taiwan dollar opened at NT$31.8, down 0.019, then briefly appreciated to NT$31.76, but spent most of the day weakening, hitting a low of NT$31.821. The intraday range was 0.061 NT$.

Looking at the major Asian currencies, the US dollar index jumped 0.4%, causing non‑US currencies to weaken across the board: the Thai baht fell 0.4%, the Singapore dollar slipped more than 0.2%, and both the Japanese yen and Chinese yuan weakened about 0.1%, while the New Taiwan dollar closed down 0.04%.

Unified Investment Advisory noted that although market focus remains on developments in the Middle East and on the Federal Reserve’s upcoming release of the September meeting minutes, the IEA’s announcement of releasing 100 million barrels from strategic reserves should help stabilize oil prices in the short term.

On the other hand, the AI boom is driving corporate investment and solid economic growth. US September ISM manufacturing new orders accelerated, and with the Q3 earnings season kicking off next week, statistical agencies are repeatedly raising profit forecasts, supporting a bullish US equity outlook and further bolstering support levels for the Taiwan stock market.
